capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

For the first part, unfold convergence to `Filter.smallSets (nhds x)`: it means that every neighborhood `U` of `x` eventually contains `closedBall x r`. Choose `ε > 0` with `ball x ε ⊆ U`. For all radii `r < ε` sufficiently near `0`, any `y ∈ closedBall x r` satisfies `dist y x ≤ r < ε`, hence lies in `U`.

For the second part, represent
\[
\operatorname{sphere}(x,\varepsilon)=\{y\mid \operatorname{dist}(y,x)=\varepsilon\}
\]
as the preimage of the closed singleton `{ε}` under the continuous function `y ↦ dist y x`. Thus the sphere is closed.

No separation assumption beyond `PseudoMetricSpace` is needed; points at distance zero are automatically contained in every neighborhood of `x`.
